description: Frozen ground truth for the ERC-20 token benchmark. All values are expected outputs from the LLMLL compiler toolchain. Re-baselined 2026-07-02 against llmll 0.14.2 after the original v0.3.0-era expectations (predating BODY-VC v0.8.0, LT-INV core/shell v0.11.0, and TRUST-PRE v0.13.0) stopped holding — see 'future_work' below for what a full 6/6-verified baseline would actually require.

matrix.rationale: result >= 0, given (pre (>= state 0)) — pure integer comparison, body-faithful
result >= 0, given (pre (>= state 0)) — pure integer comparison, body-faithful

total-supply(result) = total-supply(state) is stated but not solver-discharged: transfer's body is a no-op stub (state modeled as a single int, no real per-account transfer logic) and total-supply is called only inside the postcondition, not the body, so the assume-guarantee call-edge machinery has no call site to compose over. See 'future_work'.

amount >= 0 precondition is stated; transfer itself is def-shell (permissive, required to admit calling total-supply/balance-of, which are not in the trusted prelude) and its own body-VC falls back for the same reason as the conservation property above

amount >= 0 is a precondition (a caller obligation) with no postcondition on approve's own behavior, so under TRUST-PRE (v0.13.0) it has no effective post-level and reports as no-contract for trust-report summary purposes — this is correct, current behavior, not a gap
result >= 0 is pure integer comparison, body-faithful
same structural limitation as transfer conservation above
allowance >= amount precondition is stated; transfer-from is def-shell for the same reason as transfer
Map operations are outside the SMT theory
Conditional branch logic, not a linear arithmetic property

future_work.goal: Get transfer/transfer-from's own postconditions to genuinely verify (not just be stated), matching what this benchmark originally aspired to.
future_work.why_not_now: This benchmark models the entire ledger as a single bare int (see total-supply/balance-of's bodies, both literally `(var state)`) with no real per-account balances. transfer's body is a no-op stub; its conservation postcondition calls total-supply only inside the post clause, which the current assume-guarantee call-edge machinery doesn't compose over (it needs a real call site in the body, the way examples/payments-core/transfer.llmll actually calls debit in its body). Getting transfer to verified requires a materially richer benchmark: a real per-account balance representation and a body that actually moves value between two accounts, calling balance-of/total-supply-equivalents as part of that computation -- not just a fixture patch.
future_work.reference_pattern: examples/payments-core/transfer.llmll shows the shape this would need: a def-shell caller whose body genuinely calls a verified callee, composing to reach verified itself.

expected_weakness_check.rebaseline_note: Re-frozen against llmll 0.26.2. The AST had spelled every return type as 'returns', a key the parser ignores, so no function had a declared return type and weakness-check proposed no return-typed candidate. With 'return_type', each declared int return adds the constant candidate (lambda [...] 0). allowance (body 0, post result >= 0, no pre) is confirmed weak by it, and total-supply and balance-of are now confirmed by two candidates each. Trust and spec-coverage counts are unchanged.
expected_weakness_check.note: total-supply, balance-of and allowance carry a trivially-satisfiable post (result >= 0, satisfied by a candidate body) and are recorded as confirmed weaknesses. The other candidates report as unknown (body translation outside the checkable QF-LIA fragment), not confirmed weak. Strengthening these posts is deferred with the erc20 richer-benchmark; recording them here gives benchmark-erc20.sh teeth against a NEW weakness.
